svg.aria-label: A typesetting bench that names a molecule and checks the name. On the left the input structure lies on a specimen plate under four dial gauges, beside a card that holds its SMILES. A cabinet of type drawers sets a name in a galley, one sort per part of the name. The galley rides a rail to a separate machine, OPSIN, which reads only the type, draws the structure it reads on its own plate and cuts a key from it. At a lock whose 25 pins are set by the input's InChIKey the key either lifts every pin to the shear line, and a gate opens to a sled that files the galley in the PIN, fallback or best-effort tray, or it does not, and the galley is pushed into the reject bin. A flag on the cabinet rises when no name can be built. Numerals 1 to 6 stamped on the parts match the legend. The figure plays the six steps in turn: 1, read the structure; 2, set the name; 3, read it back; 4, check the key; 5, land on a tier; 6, withdraw what fails.

g.text: Six steps, numbered 1 to 6 on the parts and in the legend
Read the structure, set the name, read it back, check the key, land on a tier, or withdraw what fails.
Here caffeine's name has passed the key check: 25 of 25 pins match.
Step 1 of 6 · Read the structure
RDKit reads the SMILES; Orthonym finds the rings, the characteristic groups and the
stereocentres, whose CIP descriptors come from the centres labeller.
Step 2 of 6 · Set the name
Rules from the IUPAC 2013 recommendations choose the parent hydride, the prefixes,
the locants and their alphanumerical order: one sort of type per part of the name.
Step 3 of 6 · Read it back
OPSIN, a separate parser that never saw the structure, reads only the name
and builds the structure that the name describes.
Step 4 of 6 · Check the key
The InChIKey of what OPSIN read must equal the input's InChIKey letter for letter:
for caffeine all 25 pins sit level.
Step 5 of 6 · Land on a tier
The strict PIN path built this name and it read back, so it is the PIN: pin_verified.
Other names that read back land in the fallback or best-effort tray.
Step 6 of 6 · Withdraw what fails
For cis-decalin the PIN-path name (4as,8as)-decahydronaphthalene reads back with its
constitution only: 17 of 25 pins, so it is withdrawn; cis-decahydronaphthalene reads back: best_effort.
OPSIN 2.9.0

svg.text: key cut from what OPSIN read

text.tspan: : RDKit reads the SMILES; the structure is perceived: characteristic groups, rings, chains, CIP stereo.
: the IUPAC 2013 rules set the name, one sort per part of it.
: reads only the name back, draws the structure it read and cuts its key.
: 25 pins, one per letter: the read-back key must match the input's key.
: a name that fails is withdrawn; the flag rises when no name is left.
